message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—steady traffic, no major detours, and staying within speed limits—the trip usually takes **about 6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic can be heavy, add an extra hour or two. Conversely, if you’re traveling on a clear day with minimal stops, you might get there closer to the 5½‑hour mark. Always check a live navigation app for real‑time traffic updates before you hit the road.

We can provide approximate driving distance (~383 miles via I-5) and typical driving time (~6 hours). But we might also mention traffic, speed limits, etc. No function call needed. Provide answer.
